title: Clear Roadblocks QA

short.lead: The roadblocks rule and its reply check are built as plugin 2.88.0; you check that a claim like "Unity is not installed" gets blocked twice, then carries a warning.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what to do.
items: Both verify scripts pass, and the check blocks twice then warns

I ran verify.py (1345 of 1345 checks pass) and verify_tools.py (55 of 55). I also ran the branch's hook.py three times with the same roadblock claim and no probe. The first two replies were blocked ("block 1 of 2", "block 2 of 2"). The third printed the warning "a roadblock claim (i cannot) went out unchecked".

items.caption: What the check does for one user message.

items: Try it in a session on the branch build

Install the branch build, start a new session, and ask something that tempts a roadblock claim. Expect me to run a check or install the tool instead of saying it is missing. The exact steps are in Wrap-up.

changes: Rule: Roadblocks are mine to clear
One short section in the rules, with its detail file.

Check before claiming a tool or machine is missing, install what is missing, try the next route, and keep only purchases, licences, logins and destructive actions for you. The injected rules are 9,694 of 9,700 characters.
Blocks a roadblock claim twice per message, then warns.

The state file lives in the temp directory, keyed by transcript path and your message count. An unreadable transcript or state file produces a message and never blocks. HOUSE_RULES_ROADBLOCKS=off turns it off.
The #89 'untested' case now uses a four-hour suite as its reason.
Its old reason, a missing Unity editor, is exactly what the new check blocks.

unverified: No live Claude Code session has run 2.88.0 yet: the Stop hook in the session that built it is the installed 2.87.0, so every check drove the branch's hook.py directly or used fixture transcripts
Which phrases real replies use for a roadblock was not measured; the check flags a fixed list of phrases, so a roadblock worded another way goes through
The install-without-asking behaviour in bypass mode is a rule I follow, not something a hook enforces

wrapup.summary: The roadblocks rule and its end-of-reply check are built as plugin 2.88.0 and wait for your test.
